query: How can we reduce declined travel expenses?

per_column.name: expense_category
per_column.rationale: Directly identifies travel_expense rows, which is the exact segment the query targets. Values are soundly derived from short_description/ci (e.g. 'cloud service' -> cloud_service, 'hardware asset' -> hardware_asset).

per_column.name: entry_method
per_column.rationale: Manual vs automated entry is a plausible axis for error/decline analysis and is well grounded in text cues ('Automated creation' -> automated). Somewhat generic to declines but offers a real grouping dimension.

per_column.name: asset_action_type
per_column.rationale: Asset-lifecycle actions (registration, procurement, deployment) are oriented toward hardware/assets, not travel expenses, so limited leverage for THIS query. Values are mostly readable from descriptions, though similar phrasings map inconsistently (e.g. 'Procurement of new'->new_procurement vs 'creation of new'->registration).

per_column.name: has_source_id
per_column.rationale: A bare boolean derived trivially from the existing source_id column; largely redundant and generic, giving little analytical leverage on declined travel expenses. Well grounded (presence/absence of source_id).

per_column.name: ci_brand
per_column.rationale: Extracting brand from ci is reasonable and could support vendor-level comparison, but 'travel_brand' and 'cloud_vendor' are placeholder pseudo-brands rather than actual brands read from text, weakening groundedness for the travel segment relevant here.

judge.rationale: The set includes one highly relevant column (expense_category) that isolates the travel segment central to the query, plus a couple of moderately useful grouping axes (entry_method, ci_brand). Others (asset_action_type, has_source_id) are asset-focused or trivially redundant and add little leverage for reducing declined travel expenses. Most values are soundly grounded in short_description and ci text, though ci_brand introduces non-textual placeholder brand labels and asset_action_type shows some inconsistent mapping of similar phrasings.
